source: FP sweep benchmarks/sweeps/ (v0.1.5, duplicate-survivor build), 6 OSS repos x 300 commits = 1800
method: each of the 45 blocked commits of the v0.1.2 build adjudicated against the real diff; 40 by independent agents (nine batches, five each), 5 by the maintainer after one batch hit a session limit - noted because it is a weaker form of independence for those five. v0.1.3 stopped blocking two (attrs 7373d88, click b761eda), v0.1.4 seven more (attrs 74007f67d2, click 700798252a, httpx 59914c7690, starlette 100f05a66b/5ccbc62175/856c904a6d/b133ab45ad), v0.1.5 one more (click 1103c5cac2, deleted duplicate with a live survivor outside the diff) - all ten false_positive. One verdict was re-categorised on evidence: click a391797d00 false_positive -> spec_correct, because its reason claimed every deleted unit reappears in the same diff and `git grep` at that head proves test_prompt_cast_default reappears nowhere; the re-check that found this is recorded in the verdict itself. No commit is newly blocked; every other verdict is unchanged from the v0.1.2 adjudication

categories.false_positive: blocking was wrong; no oracle weakening, or compensated visibly in-diff
categories.spec_correct: blocking was defensible; oracle coverage dropped with no visible in-diff compensation
categories.unclear: cannot be decided from the diff

verdicts.reason: "Fix message passing in frozen errors" makes FrozenError set its message via __init__/super().__init__(msg); the test adds `match="can't set attribute"` to both pytest.raises blocks AND keeps/duplicates the exact-value check as `assert e.value.msg == e.value.args[0] == "can't set attribute"` in both blocks. The oracle got strictly stronger; greenwash only saw the new `match=` pattern and scored it as a downgrade.

"Only soft-deprecate hash (#1330)" removes the `warnings.warn(DeprecationWarning(...))` calls from both `attrs()` and `make_class()` in src/attr/_make.py in the same diff, so the two `test_hash_is_deprecated` tests (which assert `pytest.deprecated_call()`) test behavior that no longer exists. Production genuinely changed in a way that explains the deletion; greenwash failed to connect the src and tests hunks.

"Support legacy case of default aligning to flag_value for flag whose default=True" rewrites the tail of test_flag_value_prompt to `assert result.exit_code == 0 if expected not in (REPEAT, INVALID) else 1`, which Python parses as `assert ((exit_code == 0) if cond else 1)` — for every new REPEAT/INVALID case the exit-code check degrades to `assert 1`, an always-true truthy assertion. greenwash's EXACT_VALUE(90) -> TRUTHY(20) is literally what the diff does.

"Check for warning exception with idiomatic context manager" replaces `assert result.exit_code == 1` / `isinstance(result.exception, UserWarning)` / `"used more than once" in str(...)` with `with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="used more than once"): runner.invoke(cli, [])`. The exit_code==1 assertion only held because pyproject sets `filterwarnings = ["error"]`; inside pytest.warns the warning is recorded instead of raised, so that assertion is no longer applicable, and pytest.warns still fails if the warning type or message is absent. The oracle moved form without losing strength.

"Add regular and stress tests for ``CliRunner`` stream lifecycle and ownership" deletes the 25-line tests/test_testing_logging.py but adds a 538-line tests/test_stream_lifecycle.py in the same diff whose "Category 3: Logging interaction (issues #824, #3110)" section includes test_invoke_with_logger_and_prompt described as "the exact #824 reproducer" plus test_logging_with_cli_log_level, replacing the deleted test's coverage and removing its FIXME-weakened dual-value assertion.

"add zizmor to scan workflows" deletes .github/workflows/test-flask.yaml, which ran flask's full pytest suite against click main as a downstream integration gate, and also removes the `stress` job from tests.yaml; the only added workflow is a zizmor GitHub Actions security scanner, so real CI test coverage is removed with nothing in this diff replacing it.

"Make test echo file." moves nine echo/pager units verbatim into tests/test_utils_2/ (all de-escalated to info as moves once the relocation credits could see them), but it ALSO deletes test_prompt_cast_default outright: `git grep -l "def test_prompt_cast_default" a391797d00` finds the unit nowhere at that commit's head. A real oracle (prompt default cast to int, isinstance assert) vanished with no copy, no move and no replacement; the next-day commit 1103c5cac2 re-added it, which reads as an accidental deletion caught. The original adjudication said "every flagged unit exists verbatim in the new files in the same diff" - that was wrong for this unit, discovered when the v0.1.5 duplicate search went looking for the surviving copy and proved there was none. Blocking is correct.

"Fix broken fish completion and multiline help string" rewrites FishComplete.format_completion from a 3-line newline-delimited frame to a comma/tab frame, updates the parametrized format cases to match, and then deletes test_fish_multiline_help_complete outright. The new code still escapes newlines (help_.replace("\n", "\\n")) but nothing in the post-commit tests/test_shell_completion.py exercises a multi-line help string any more, so coverage of the very bug being fixed drops with no replacement in this diff.

"Remove duplicate test" drops the single line `assert value is not True` from test_unset_sentinel, but the same test body (unchanged, immediately below) contains `real_values` including `True` and loops `assert value != real_value; assert value is not real_value`. The removed assertion is exactly subsumed by retained coverage in the same unit, so the oracle is not weakened.

"Fix test_edit to work with BSD sed" changes the test's own input from `"a
b"` to `"a
b
"` in the same hunk, so the expected value necessarily becomes `"aTest
bTest
"`. It remains a single exact `==` comparison (greenwash itself notes "no change in assertion strength"); the input change that explains the new expectation is visible three lines above in the same diff.

"pager doesn't close std streams" adds a `_SkipClose` wrapper in src/click/_termui_impl.py so `_nullpager` now yields `_SkipClose(stream)` instead of the stream itself; `assert pager is created[0]` is therefore impossible by construction and is replaced with the stronger, on-point `assert not stream.closed` plus the retained `stream.getvalue() == styled_text`, and a new end-to-end `test_with_echo_via_pager` is added in tests/test_testing.py in the same diff.

"Fix broken fish completion and multiline help string" deletes test_fish_multiline_help_complete (50 lines) outright, and nothing in the diff replaces it — the updated parametrized fish cases only cover the new "plain,a
plain,b	bee
" comma/tab format, not the multi-line help escaping (`item.help.replace("
", "\n")`) that the deleted test asserted. Real coverage drop with no in-diff compensation; a reviewer would allowlist it as a revert of the regressing PR's test.

"Add parametrized tests for `should_strip_ansi`" does not invert polarity: `assert not should_strip_ansi(stream=...)` was replaced by `assert click._compat._is_jupyter_kernel_output(stream=...)`, a different predicate whose True is semantically the same claim, and the same diff adds a 36-case parametrized `test_should_strip_ansi` covering isatty/is_jupyter/color. Coverage rises, not falls.

"add codespell pre-commit hook" is a spelling fix that edits the fixture and the assertion in lockstep: the sentinel is changed at its definition (default=/help="you won't see me") and in the matching `assert "you won't see me" not in result.output`. The assertion still checks that the same sentinel never reaches output, so strength is unchanged.

"separate copy per call" moves `original.copy()` from decoration time into the wrapper in src/flask/ctx.py, and the same diff deletes the greenlet dependency from pyproject.toml while replacing both `TestGreenletContextCopying` tests with `test_copy_context_thread`, which drives `copy_current_request_context` across a 10-item ThreadPoolExecutor map and asserts the same current_app/path/args/session invariants — equivalent (arguably stronger) coverage added in the same diff.

"remove egg test" deletes test_egg_installed_paths and the install_egg fixture (37 lines of conftest) while the only production change in src/flask/scaffold.py is a comment edit ('points to the .egg or .zip file' -> 'points to the .zip file'); the loader.archive branch it exercised still exists and nothing in this diff replaces the coverage. Deleting for environmental reasons (Python 3.12 drops setuptools) is exactly the allowlist case.

"push preserved contexts in correct order" changes src/flask/testing.py from `while self._new_contexts: cm = self._new_contexts.pop()` to a forward `for cm in self._new_contexts`, and the flagged test is renamed test_redirect_keep_session -> test_redirect_session in the same diff, rewritten to assert the newly-correct ordering (session["redirect"] and session["target"] both True after follow_redirects) rather than removed.

The commit is exactly "remove unicode host test" — a single file, 21 pure deletions of `test_environ_for_valid_idna_completes`, with no production change and no replacement test anywhere in the diff. Oracle coverage for IDNA HTTP_HOST handling drops with nothing in this diff compensating, so blocking is greenwash doing its documented job and a reviewer would allowlist it.

"remove werkzeug host tests" is 48 pure deletions in one test file, no production change, no replacement anywhere in the diff. The coverage moved to the upstream werkzeug project, which no diff analyser can see. Blocking is the documented behaviour; a reviewer allowlists it.

"revert cli test change" is test-only and undoes the strengthening from e82db2c: `assert "HEAD" not in output` plus `assert "OPTIONS" not in output` collapse back to the single narrower `assert "GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, POST" not in output`, and the `_automatic_options` filter in test_all_urls is dropped too. No production file is touched and nothing in this diff restores the lost coverage.

"test `parse_header_links` via public api (#3061)" changes `assert parse_header_links(value) == expected` to `assert all(link in all_links for link in expected)` — exact equality becomes a subset check, so extra/incorrect links go undetected and the `("", [])` parameter case becomes vacuously true. The production edit is a behavior-preserving rewrite of `Response.links` into a dict comprehension and the added `test_parse_header_links_no_link` only covers the missing-header case, so nothing in this diff restores the lost exactness.

"Use httpx public API for 'test_content' tests" swaps every `encode_request(...)` call for `httpx.Request(method, url, ...)` in the same hunks; the Host header appears in the expectations because a real Request populates it, which is why `{'Transfer-Encoding': 'chunked'}` becomes `{'Host': 'www.example.com', 'Transfer-Encoding': 'chunked'}`. The assertions stay full-dict equality (test_empty_content even gains `Content-Length: 0`), so the rewrites are compensated in-diff by the visible change of subject under test.

"Drop private imports from test_exceptions.py (#2571)" deletes test_httpx_exceptions_exposed, whose oracle was that every Exception subclass in the private httpx._exceptions module is re-exported on httpx; the surviving test_httpcore_all_exceptions_mapped only checks that httpcore exception *names* appear in httpx, so an httpx-defined exception left unexported is no longer caught, and nothing in this diff restores that check.

"Drop private import of 'encode_request' in test_multipart" rewrites the test to use the public `httpx.Request` API with a fixed BOUNDARY. Both oracles survive in the same hunk: the exact dict equality `request.headers == {Host, Content-Type, Transfer-Encoding: chunked}` (now stricter, it also pins Host) and the exact byte equality on `request.content`. Only the incidental `assert isinstance(stream, typing.Iterable)` scaffolding for the removed private API is gone.

"Ensure JSON representation is compact" changes encode_json to `json_dumps(json, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False)` in httpx/_content.py in the same diff, which directly explains Content-Length 18 -> 17. The flagged edit `response.json() == {"hello": "world"}` -> `str(response.json()) == "{'hello': 'world'}"` is at least as strict (string repr also pins key order), so no coverage was lost.

"Adapt test_response_decode_text_using_autodetect for chardet 6.0" turns `assert response.encoding == "ISO-8859-1"` into `assert response.encoding in ("ISO-8859-1", "WINDOWS-1252")`. The expectation is genuinely widened to accept two values and nothing in this diff (no production change, only a comment) replaces the lost precision — the justification lives in an external dependency's version bump, exactly the case a reviewer would allowlist.

"Revert \"Raise `TypeError` on invalid query params. (#2523)\"" deletes the `raise TypeError(f"Expected str, int, float, bool, or None...")` from primitive_value_to_str in httpx/_utils.py in the same diff, so test_invalid_query_params (a `pytest.raises(TypeError, match=...)` on exactly that message) is asserting behavior that no longer exists. The production change explaining the deletion is right there in the diff; greenwash failed to connect them.

"Drop private imports from test_decoders.py (#2570)" rewrites the decoder tests onto the public API, and the same diff compensates: test_byte_chunker/test_text_chunker are replaced by new chunk_size=7 cases in tests/models/test_responses.py (test_iter_raw_with_chunksize, test_iter_text_with_chunk_size). The line-decoder 'rewrites' are just the merge of the old decode()+flush() split into one iter_lines() list — e.g. ['a','','b'] + ['c'] becomes ['a','','b','c'] — same expected output.

"Add URL parsing tests from WHATWG (#3188)" rewrites `validate_path` in httpx/_urlparse.py — the `//` and `:` checks are re-guarded under `not has_scheme and not has_authority` and both messages are reworded to "Relative URLs cannot have a path starting with ..." — so the expectation edit tracks a visible production change in the same diff; the assertions keep identical strength (still `pytest.raises(httpx.InvalidURL)` plus exact message equality), and the diff adds tests/models/test_whatwg.py with a 9.7k-line WHATWG conformance corpus.

"Cleanup unneccessary test case (#3375)" is a test-only diff (23 deletions, no production change) that removes test_netrc_auth_nopassword. Its asserts duplicated test_netrc_auth_credentials_do_not_exist, but it was the only test constructing httpx.NetRCAuth against the passwordless .netrc-nopassword fixture on Python 3.11+, and nothing in this diff replaces that; a reviewer would allowlist it rather than call it a tool bug.

"test `same_origin` via public api (#3062)" replaces `assert not same_origin(o1, o2)` with an assertion about redirect headers — a different subject entirely, in a test-only diff. THREATMODEL "what greenwash cannot catch" #7 states that a private-API check rewritten against the public API blocks deliberately, because the de-escalation that would excuse it would also excuse swapping an exact comparison for a wide approx().

"fix tests" is a one-line, test-only diff that rewrites `Text.from_ansi("
Hello
World

").plain` from `"Hello
World

"` to `"
Hello
World

"` with no production change anywhere in the commit; only by reading the two preceding commits (33d56f1 "tests" added the assertion, f261bfa touched only whitespace in rich/ansi.py) can you tell the original expectation was a copy-paste mistake rather than the intended spec, so a diff-scoped analyser blocking an expectation bent to match current behaviour is doing its documented job.

"test fixes" is test-only: it deletes test_no_nested_live outright and rewrites several hardcoded ANSI expectations to match new output. The cause is an upstream pygments change, outside the diff, so the expectations are bent to match current behaviour with nothing in-diff explaining why. Exactly the shape the rule exists to surface; a reviewer allowlists it.

"Return explicit origin in CORS response when credentials are allowed (#3137)" replaces the `has_cookie` condition in starlette/middleware/cors.py with `self.allow_credentials`, so the cookie-triggered behavior the flagged tests asserted no longer exists; test_cors_allowed_origin_does_not_leak_between_credentialed_requests is renamed to ..._between_requests and keeps its three-request leak check, and test_cors_credentialed_requests_return_specific_origin's oracle moves into test_cors_allow_all (allow_credentials=True), which the same diff changes to assert access-control-allow-origin == "https://example.org" instead of "*".

"Set `Content-Type` instead of `Content-Range` on multi-range responses (#3142)" changes starlette/responses.py to write the multipart boundary into content-type rather than content-range, so the flagged assert in test_file_response_multi_small_chunk_size necessarily changes; the same hunk adds `assert "content-range" not in headers` and `assert headers["content-type"].startswith("multipart/byteranges; boundary=")`, and the sibling range tests gain the same pair — coverage goes up, not down.
